predictions.question: 四周期单 q 条纹只改变整体相位，保持 A=1 时，两个非零卫星的 |F|² 如何变化？
choices: 每个仍为 1/4，但实空间图案和复系数相位可变
强度必随 cos²φ 变化
predictions.explanation: q 与 −q 在 N=4 的这组条纹中是不同臂；F(q)=e^(iφ)/2，所以每个强度恒为 1/4。自共轭边界点只有一个实自由度，是不同情形。

predictions.question: N=3、q=(1/3,1/3) 的单 q 斜条纹，矩形周期为 3×3。最小平移指数是多少？
predictions.explanation: 保留平移满足 tx+ty=0 mod 3，共有 3 个。声明平移群有 9 个元素，故指数为 9/3=3。矩形超胞容纳了三个最小斜胞。

lessons.title: From a q to a real visible multi-arm pattern
lessons.summary: differentiates wavevector star, conjugate pairing, real representation space from the currently active mode.

sections.title: First declare the mother lattice and mode basis
sections.text: Use a square layer with one dimensionless scalar per site. Order r=(x,y) with x varying first and y second, embedding the plane at z=0 in three dimensions. C₄ᵥ operations do not reverse the scalar’s sign; it can represent occupancy deviations or out-of-plane displacement amplitudes. Actual crystal modes not specified here require a separate construction.

sections.title: uses point operations to construct q stars
sections.text: Reduce numerators of q modulo N: arms differing by a parent reciprocal vector are equivalent. For N=4 and (1,0)/4, C₄ successively produces (0,1)/4, (3,0)/4 and (0,3)/4. The star lists symmetry-related possible components; a particular pattern need not activate every arm.

sections.title: Conjugate pairing makes the field real
sections.text: Non-self-conjugated q and −q provide a pair of cos/sin real basis. The input phase controls the combination of these two real basis. A self-conjugate point q≡−q has only one real basis; for example (1,1)/2 of N=2, whose sin mode is zero at all lattice points.

sections.title: Replay the representation construction and submit a subspace
sections.text: Replay shows integer rotations, star arms, orthonormal real bases, pairwise superposition, actual translations and projection reconstruction. The assignment targets the space spanned by the complete star and permits nonsingular internal basis changes; submitting only the current field generally does not span the full star.
sections.formula: P=B(B†B)⁻¹B†; B→BM (M reversible) does not change P

lessons.title: supercell , pattern stabilizer and translation domain
lessons.summary: Apply group elements to the actual pattern one by one to check the preservation of symmetry and the true inclusion relationship of the finite group.

sections.title: compatible supercell The first is the periodic boundary condition
sections.text: Select N=2, 3, and 4 for this experiment to ensure that the input is rational and wavevector is compatible with N×N supercell . Actual patterns may have shorter periods. Checking that q · t is an integer for all non-zero Fourier components finds that the translation is preserved; the phase-cancelled zero modes should not continue to limit the period.
sections.formula: f(r+t)=f(r) ⇔ e^(2πiq·t)=1（ for each non-zero Fourier component)

sections.title: The rectangular cell is not necessarily the smallest
sections.text: Diagonal stripes f=cos[2π(x+y)/3] have separate x and y periods 3, but translation (1,−1) preserves the pattern. Thus 3×3 is a compatible rectangular cell, while a minimal oblique cell has area index only 3. The interface reports rectangular periods and the exact translation index separately.

sections.title: stabilizer acts on the entire pattern
sections.text: enumerates 8N² abstract elements in (Z_N×Z_N)⋊C₄ᵥ, and compares D(g)f with f for each site value. H includes a combination of point operations and translations; just checking whether q is fixed, or just pure point operations, will miss the phase condition of the pattern.

sections.title: Use graphs to test inclusion relationships and then count symmetrical related states
sections.text: The graph shows G, translation group T, current stabilizer H, intersection H∩T and the trivial group, merging identical subgroups. Edges denote actual inclusions. The full pattern count is |G|/|H|, whereas translation-generated antiphase domains number |T|/|H∩T|. A finite quotient group does not replace standard three-dimensional space-group labels.

lessons.title: Real space superposition, satellite weights and verifiable predictions
lessons.summary: corresponds the phase and amplitude of the mode to Fourier weights, distinguishing computational models from real diffraction experiments.

sections.title: Fixed Fourier convention
sections.text: Use a negative exponent and 1/N² normalization. The plot's k=x+Ny indexes the reciprocal grid; the table gives actual 2D q and complex coefficients. A real-valued field requires coefficients at negative q to be complex conjugates.

sections.title: Amplitude and phase experiment of single q
sections.text: For mutually different q and −q, A cos(2πq·r+φ) has intensity A²/4 in both arms. Translation changes the phase of the complex coefficients but not the two intensities. Try to predict the effect of the phase slider first, and then look at the pattern, complex coefficients, and intensity.

sections.title: Double q Put the weights on different arms
sections.text: Different conjugate pairs occupy different reciprocal points, so relative amplitudes change arm weights. Relative phases can change real-space patterns and stabilizers without changing individual non-self-conjugate-arm intensities. Select the unequal-amplitude preset and test whether fourfold symmetry survives.

sections.title: Integrate teaching prediction into material projects
sections.text: reports the declared parent lattice, mode, q-star, stabilizer and translational index before taking the mode weights to the diffraction or dynamic structure factor module. Real experiments also require atomic species, scattering factors, Q·u, magnetic polarization, and instrument geometry. The pattern that symmetry allows does not automatically become the lowest energy phase.
sections.formula: Experimental intensity requires structure factors; scalar mode |F|² only provides relative Fourier weights

exercises.title: gradually constructs four-period stripes real representation
exercises.prompt: uses N=4, q=(1,0)/4 single q presets and uses playback to check.

steps.explanation: C₄(1,0)=(0,1). Act again to get the negative x arm, and again to get the negative y arm.

steps.prompt: How many different arms does this complete set of q stars have?
steps.hint: Wave vectors are equivalent only if they differ by an integer parent reciprocal-lattice vector.

steps.prompt: What is the real subspace dimension of the complete star?
steps.hint: Two pairs of non-self-conjugated arms, each pair providing cos and sin.
steps.explanation: Each conjugate pair provides two real degrees of freedom, totaling 4; instead of arbitrarily assigning two independent real numbers to each arm.

steps.prompt: Multiply these four basis vectors by an invertible 4×4 matrix. How should the assignment be scored?
steps.hint: compares spanned subspaces rather than matrices to be identical item by item.
choices: Pass if the vectors span the same space
Fails as long as any column is different
steps.explanation: Invertible internal basis changes preserve the column space and orthogonal projector.

exercises.title: Find the minimum translation index from oblique stripes
exercises.prompt: adopts the single q presets of N=3 and q=(1,1)/3. Write the conditions first and then verify stabilizer .

steps.hint: Let the Fourier phase factor equal to 1 first.

steps.prompt: How many translations survive within the declared 3×3 translation group?
steps.explanation: Three translations form H∩T, which is closed and contains the identity element.

steps.prompt: What are the minimum translation index and the area of ​​the compatible rectangular cell respectively?
steps.hint: index is calculated by |T|/|H∩T|, and the rectangular periods are calculated separately.
steps.explanation: is 9/3=3; the respective periods of x and y are 3, and the area of the rectangular cell is 9.

steps.prompt: Limited quotient group The order of G is 72, and the calculated order of H is 12. What is the number of all symmetry related patterns?
steps.explanation: 72/12=6, of which only 3 are obtained by translation from the current pattern; the rest are from different orientations.

exercises.title: Derivation of satellite weights from real field and checking constraints
exercises.prompt: starts with the single q stripe of N=4 and compares the checkerboard and double q stripes.

steps.prompt: For non-self-conjugate single-q stripes with A=1, what is each nonzero satellite’s intensity?
steps.hint: Write cosine as two complex exponents.
steps.explanation: Each Fourier coefficient has modulus 1/2, so each intensity is 1/4.

steps.prompt: What should be the sum of all Fourier intensities at this time?
steps.hint: Parseval equates this to the real field mean square.
steps.explanation: has two arms of strength 1/4, which sum to 1/2, equal to the discrete mean square of the four-period cosine.

steps.prompt: N=2's checkerboard changes φ from 0 to 90°, why does the field disappear?
steps.hint: Its q and −q vectors modulo reciprocal lattice are the same.
choices: proves that all satellites are independent of phase
sin mode is zero at these grid points, the only real mode times cosφ
because group order number becomes zero
steps.explanation: The self-conjugated arm has only one real degree of freedom, so the conclusion that the two mutually different arms have fixed strengths cannot be followed.

steps.prompt: The scalar mode |F|² has been found. Is it equal to the true displacement diffraction intensity?
steps.hint: Real scattering also depends on atomic and experimental geometry.
choices: also requires structure factor, Q·u and other information
steps.explanation: Here are the mode Fourier weights; real atomic scattering, polarization and geometric factors are not included.

cases.title: Stripes and double-q order in a square layer
cases.kind: An occupation-pattern teaching model for layered materials
cases.summary: Comparing single q stripes and equal-amplitude double q cross patterns on the same square parent lattice, tracking stabilizer , orientation changes and translational domains.
cases.assumption: has only one scalar deviation per site and no real chemical structure and energy parameters; it cannot be used to identify the ground state of any specific material.

cases.title: Checkerboards and antiphase domains: exchange of two sublattices
cases.kind: two-period occupancy or vertical displacement model
cases.summary: Through the self-conjugated boundary point of N=2, observe the translational exchange of two patterns of primitive cell once, and understand the single real degree of freedom of the self-conjugated wavevector .
cases.assumption: Mode values represent occupation deviations or displacement amplitudes, not occupancies directly. The N=2 site action is nonfaithful; full abstract finite-group counts are retained.

cases.title: diagonal stripes: from supercell pattern to satellite peaks
cases.summary: Compare a 3×3 rectangular supercell with the minimal translation cell of index 3. Use Fourier weights to predict satellite intensities before and after phase changes.
cases.assumption: fixes the square mother lattice and scalar mode, omitting the true structure factor; does not treat the compatible cell as a three-dimensional standard unit cell, and does not output any space group label.
links: Inelastic scattering and the dynamic structure factor
